title: Label-free method for anti-glucopeptide antibody detection in Multiple Sclerosis
author: Real-Fernández, Rossi, et al.

steps.title: Thaw and dilute serum
steps.instruction: Thaw human serum samples to ambient temperature, then dilute each sample either 1:100 or 1:50 in running buffer.

steps.title: Set SPR flow conditions
steps.instruction: Configure the SPR instrument to a flow rate of 30 µL/min and ensure the glucopeptide antigen is immobilized on the sensor surface.

steps.title: Inject diluted serum (association)
steps.instruction: Inject each diluted serum sample (high‑positive patient and healthy control) over the immobilized glucopeptide in triplicate, using contact times ranging from 60 s to 240 s (optimal: 240 s at 1:50 dilution).

substeps.instruction: Load 150 µL of diluted sample (equivalent to 3 µL of patient serum) per injection.
Maintain the flow rate at 30 µL/min during association.

steps.title: Monitor dissociation
steps.instruction: Immediately after each association phase, switch to running buffer at 30 µL/min and monitor dissociation for 60 s.

steps.title: Record sensorgrams
steps.instruction: Capture the interaction as a sensorgram and register the response 15 s after the end of each sample injection; report responses in resonance units (RU) as the difference between reference and active channels.

steps.title: Regenerate sensor surface
steps.instruction: After each sample injection, regenerate the surface with two consecutive 60 s pulses of 100 mM NaOH solution to remove all bound material.

steps.title: Limit number of cycles
steps.instruction: Do not exceed 100 measurements per channel during a single experimental series.

steps.title: Validate assay performance
steps.instruction: Assess analytical variability by repeatedly testing a high‑positive serum diluted 1:50: perform 15 consecutive runs in one assay (within‑assay) and 12 runs on separate days (once per week, between‑assay); ensure coefficients of variation (SE/mean) remain below 5 %.

steps.title: Include controls regularly
steps.instruction: Run the positive control (high‑positive serum, 1:50 dilution) and a negative control every 15 sample measurements to verify probe stability over many cycles.
